question: An engineer must configure multiple EPGs on a single access port in a large Cisco ACI fabric without using VMM integration. The relevant access policies and tenant policies have been created. A single AAEP is used to configure the access ports in the fabric. Which two additional steps must be taken to complete the configuration? (Choose two.)
options: The EPGs must link directly to the corresponding AAEP.
A contract must be defined between the EPGs.
The EPGs must be configured as static ports.
The corresponding bridge domains must be configured in legacy mode.
The EPGs must be linked to the correct physical domain.
theory: Without VMM integration, an EPG can only be deployed onto an access port through static port binding, so each EPG that should use a given AAEP-managed port must be explicitly configured as a static port on that interface/VLAN. In addition, the EPG's domain association must point at a physical domain (not a VMM domain) so the fabric knows which VLAN pool/encapsulation is valid on that port — the AAEP alone only groups infrastructure policies and doesn't itself carry the EPG-to-VLAN mapping. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 4 — ACI Access Policies and Static Port Binding)
